newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco announces bid for 2008 Olympic Games.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco announces bid for 2008 Olympic Games.

text.p: San Francisco will enter a bid for the summer Olympic Games of 2008, joining a long list of other U.S. cities eager to host the games, the local organising committee said on Wednesday.
The Bay Area Sports Organising Committee said it raised the $100,000 due on May 1 to enter San Francisco into the initial bidding process.
A number of American cities, including Cincinnati, Boston, Houston, New York and Seattle, have also expressed interest in hosting the 2008 summer games.
To be considered, bidders must pay a fee of $100,000 to the U.S. Olympic Committee by the May 1 deadline.
If the committee decides to submit a U.S. city for the games, it would review the bids and recommend one of them to the International Olympics Committee, which will make the final selection in 2001.
California state Senator Quentin Kopp, an Independent who chairs the local sports organising committee, said over a dozen San Francisco area companies and individuals helped raise the $100,000.

"The generous contributions by Bay Area businesses demonstrate the strong local enthusiasm and support for hosting the 2008 Summer Olympic Games," Kopp said in a statement. "I believe we have an outstanding chance of being selected."
Atlanta hosted the 1996 games and the United States also hosted the summer games in Los Angeles in 1984 and the winter games in Lake Placid, New York, in 1980.
